title: Bauhaus Dessau - Wikipedia
content: # Bauhaus Dessau. **Bauhaus Dessau**, also **Bauhaus-Building Dessau**, is a building-complex in Dessau-Roßlau. The building was constructed between 1925 and 1926 according to plans by Walter Gropius as a school building for the Bauhaus School of Art, Design and Architecture. The building itself and the Masters' Houses that were built in the immediate vicinity established the reputation of the Bauhaus as an "icon of modernism".*[not verified in body*]. Since 1996, the building complex has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Bauhaus and its Sites in Weimar, Dessau and Bernau, which also includes the Haus am Horn, the art school building and the main building of the Bauhaus University in Weimar, the Masters' Houses in Dessau, and since 2017, the Laubenganghäuser there as well as the ADGB Trade Union School in Bernau. Between 1925 and 1932, various other buildings by Bauhaus architects were also constructed in Dessau, including the Törten housing estate, the employment office and the Kornhaus restaurant.

title: Bauhaus Museum Dessau - Locations
content: The Bauhaus Museum Dessau is a building within a building – a bar of concrete that appears to be suspended in mid-air, encased within a glass shell. In an open international competition with 831 entries submitted from all over the world, the jury selected the concept proposed by Addenda Architects, a young architectural office in Barcelona, at the end of 2015. Located in the centre of Dessau, the Bauhaus Museum creates both a boundary and a connection between urban space and nature, between shopping centres and a public park. Depending on the light situation, the surroundings are reflected to varying degrees in the building’s glass façade, which sometimes becomes transparent. In this way, attention is drawn to the building’s connection with both the city and the natural environment. A delivery area, offices, and the museum communications department are housed under the cantilever at the building’s northern end, and a space for temporary exhibitions at the southern end.

title: Bauhaus - Visit Dessau
content: # Bauhaus Dessau. Dessau is the town with the closest associations to the Bauhaus. From the Kornhaus on the Elbe to the Employment Office and Törten Housing Estate, Bauhaus architecture is omnipresent. Bauhaus Museum Dessau, which opened in 2019, shows the world’s second-largest collection of Bauhaus exhibits and tells the story of the Bauhaus as a school. At a glance: Bauhaus / Bauhaus Museum Dessau / Törten Housing Estate / Kornhaus / Employment Office. ## The Bauhaus. This is probably one of the most-photographed buildings in Germany and stands more than any other as a symbol of Modernism – the Bauhaus Building, the home of the eponymous school from 1925 to 1932. Today, it houses the Bauhaus Foundation (*Stiftung Bauhaus*) and is a place of research, teaching and design, exhibitions and concerts – and a place that no visitor to Dessau should miss. Three semi-detached houses for the Bauhaus masters and a single house for the director were built at the same time as the Bauhaus building.

title: Bauhaus Dessau Architecture Guide - Chisel & Mouse
content: # BAUHAUS DESSAU ARCHITECTURE: WALTER GROPIUS AND THE BUILDING THAT DEFINED MODERNISM. The **Bauhaus Dessau** is the most important school building of the twentieth century, and one of the most influential works of architecture ever constructed. Designed by **Walter Gropius** (1883–1969) and completed in **1926**, it was built to house the **Bauhaus** — the school of art, craft, and design that Gropius had founded in Weimar in 1919 and that, in its brief fourteen-year existence, reshaped the visual culture of the modern world. Students at the Dessau Bauhaus lived in the building, worked in it, designed its furniture and fittings, and looked at it every day from every angle as a model of what architecture could be. The building has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 1996, part of a designation that also includes the Masters' Houses on Ebertallee and the earlier Bauhaus buildings in Weimar.

The Bauhaus, now a UNESCO World Heritage site, was a legendary college of art and design, founded in Weimar, Germany in 1919. It was started by architect Walter Gropius, who wanted to create a new design language based around his ideas of "form follows function", and that simplistic design could be beautiful. Although the school was closed by the Nazis in 1933, his ideas continued to resonate across the world, making it arguably the most influential artistic house of the 20th century.
